kind: exit (witness): flip from one side of the tipping count to the other
condition_en: In one constructed example, the rule is reversed and kept for one round before it is rebuilt: the lead crosses the tipping count, the push is not taken back, and from then on the other side is the one held. One example only; no general condition is given.
condition_zh: 在一个构造出来的例子里：把规则反过来，并在规则重定之前维持一轮，领先的一方就越过了临界数目；这一推没有被收回，此后被撑住的是另一边。只是一个例子，没有给出一般条件。
evidence: experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/RuleCapture.lean, namespace Reversed (l.847-864). not_absorbed, docstring: "Before it the configuration is locked; after it, from step 1 on, neither the share nor the rule rises at any step, and the rule after the first reading step is below the rule before the perturbation." Statement (closed, no hypotheses): `Locked order favours (threshold hi lo) (twoToOne, hi) ∧ (∀ k, order.le (course (1 + k + 1)).1 (course (1 + k)).1 ∧ order.le (course (1 + k + 1)).2 (course (1 + k)).2) ∧ ¬ order.le hi (course 2).2`. locked_down: `Locked (reverse order) disfavours (threshold hi lo) (course 1)`, docstring "After one step under the reversed rule, the course is locked the other way." Module docstring, same file: "A perturbation that reverses the direction is not absorbed in general: held for one step before the reading, it carries the share across the threshold of the reading and locks the course the other way". Record theories/becoming/results/records/capture-through-the-rule.md, Does not show (Counterexample): "the share crosses the threshold, the course is locked the other way, neither share nor rule rises again". Atlas exit strength: "witness".
note: Both ends are the locked condition (for one side before, for the other after) and no loss outside the rule is counted, so by the holds-itself test this is a flip inside that place, not an arrow. One direction, one constructed example (two to one, a rule with a tipping count at parity, the reversed rule held one round): both_ways false, and no general condition for the flip. The one both_ways vote among the three readers has no support in the statement.
fixed_why: The decision itself survives: inside holds-itself, strength witness, one direction only. I read Reversed.not_absorbed and its companion locked_down: the start is Locked for the favoured side, the end is Locked the other way (locked_down) with neither side's standing nor the rule rising again, and no loss outside the rule appears anywhere in the statement. That is exactly the flip the holds-itself test keeps inside the place; the end is settled, so it is not several-ways, and nothing is read of a loss, so it is not cost-counts. No arrow was wrongly withheld. Two things need correcting. (1) condition_en reads as a general rule ('A reversed rule, kept until the lead crosses the tipping count, is not undone') while condition_zh carries the caveat that it is one constructed example; the Lean has no variables at all (a closed statement about twoToOne, hi, lo and the schedule 'late'), and the module only says a reversing push 'is not absorbed in general'. The English must carry the same witness marking as the Chinese, or a witness is passed off as a condition. (2) 'The other side holds' is not in not_absorbed's own statement; it is locked_down's. The law field should name both, since the atlas exit's 'locked the other way from step 1' rests on locked_down.

law: Becoming.RuleCapture.uniform_locks (bound shown tight by the witness Becoming.RuleCapture.Second.second_exact)
condition_en: Where the rebuilt rule favours the same side at every size of lead, any start is held after the rule's second rebuilding; one rebuilding may not be enough.
condition_zh: 只要重新定出的规则在任何领先程度下都偏向同一边，不论从哪里起步，到规则第二次重定之后就被撑住；只重定一次未必够。
evidence: Lean statement, experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/RuleCapture.lean (uniform_locks, l.291-296): docstring "Where the reading favours at every share, every course is locked from the step after its second reading step, whatever its start: share and rule perturbed, the rule against the reading, included." Statement: `(uniform : ∀ x g, favours (h x g)) {c : S × R} {r r' : Nat} (first : reads r = true) (second : reads r' = true) (lt : r < r') : Locked M favours h (paced f h reads c (r' + 1))`. Tightness, same file (Second.second_exact): "The course is not locked at step 1, the step after its first reading step; its rule falls across its second reading step; it is locked at step 2." Record theories/becoming/results/records/capture-through-the-rule.md, law 5: "every course, whatever its start, is locked from the step after its second reading step, so only a change of the law, of how the rule reads or of the selection, leaves."
note: The law is an implication with no converse, so sufficient; the exactness is of the bound of two (one constructed example), not an iff. Its premise is already the holds-itself condition (the rule is rebuilt from its results and favours one side at every lead); its start is ANY configuration, the already-locked ones included, and the statement does not describe the start as several ways in use or as shaping that pays. So the law says how fast the hold sets in, not a change from another listed place. Two readers drew several-ways -> holds-itself and one shaping-pays -> holds-itself; neither origin is in the Lean statement (the atlas's own 'from' is 'a course from any start ... not necessarily locked at the step after its first reading step'). Drawn as an arrow it would read as 'several ways tip into a hold', which this law does not show.

condition_en: the rule comes to register what is used up, and stops favouring the winners past a limit
condition_zh: 规则开始把用掉的东西算进去，用掉的超过一定限度后，就不再偏向原来的赢家
evidence: Lean, experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/ClosedCapture.lean line 287-295, docstring: "Where the rule read favours at no configuration whose loss is at least `N`, and every step adds at least one to the loss, at the step after every reading step `r` with `N ≤ b + r` the rule in force does not favour: the course is not locked there, whatever the share." note: Destination is cost-counts, not felt: the law's conclusion is that the rule in force does not favour (turned), which is cost-counts' test word for word ("not locked there; turned"); felt is for laws that do not yet say the rule has turned. The law does not say the rule then holds the other way, only that it stops favouring. The FROM end is carried by the exit's place in the atlas (it drops the premise Unread of this dynamic), not by a premise in the Lean statement: the theorem holds from any start (a, b, g), locked or not. The change is a change of how the rule is set (a different rule-setting that registers the loss), not something the closed loop does by itself; 02-MAP#t7 keeps open that this is "one sufficient way out, not shown the only one". Two of three readers agree on judged-inside -> cost-counts.

condition_en: a rule that favoured winners is re-set from what is used up, never favouring them past a limit
condition_zh: 原本偏向赢家的规则，改按用掉的东西来重定，用掉的一过某个限度，就不再偏向他们
evidence: Lean, experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/GrammarRegularity.lean lines 346-356. Docstring: "along the joined two-level step with any reading `h` that favours at no configuration whose loss is past `N`, with a reading step `r` past the bound, from a start whose rule favours, the line under the class of favouring or not is not unending: past the reading step the rule no longer favours". Statement: `(accrues : Accrues fB) {N : Nat} (turns : ∀ p g, N ≤ p.2 → ¬ favours (h p g)) ... (at_r : reads r = true) (past : N ≤ b + r) (start : favours g) : ¬ «不穷» (Law.step (Pace.step (join fA fB) h reads)) (favouredAlike favours) ((a, b), g, 0)`; the proof term applies `turned_by_loss`. Record theories/becoming/results/records/rules-that-change-themselves-in-the-grammar.md law 4: "along a joined step whose reading favours at no loss past a bound, with a reading step past it, the line under favouring or not from a favouring start is not unending". dynamics.json exit 2: strength "sufficient", drops "closedcapture-unread".
note: The same arrow as exit 1, stated in the theory's general grammar and derived from turned_by_loss: on the map ONE arrow carrying two laws, not a second arrow. Its start premise is only that the rule favours at the start (`start : favours g`), weaker than a locked or judged-inside start; the from end is carried by the exit's home (it drops Unread of this dynamic), not by a premise. Its conclusion (the favouring does not go on without end) is weaker than exit 1's (not favouring at the step after every re-setting past the limit). The law also needs what is used up to grow at every step and a re-setting to come after the limit is passed. It is a change made to how the rule is set, one sufficient way out, not shown the only one.
fixed_why: The decision (arrow, judged-inside to cost-counts, one way, sufficient) stands for the same reasons as exit 1: GrammarRegularity.lean lines 346-356, `theorem loss_ends_line ... (accrues : Accrues fB) {N : Nat} (turns : ∀ p g, N ≤ p.2 → ¬ favours (h p g)) ... (at_r : reads r = true) (past : N ≤ b + r) (start : favours g) : ¬ «不穷» (Law.step (Pace.step (join fA fB) h reads)) (favouredAlike favours) ((a, b), g, 0)`, and its proof term applies turned_by_loss. What I fix is the condition. As written ("the same change stated in the base grammar: past that limit the favouring of the winners ends") it does not stand alone ("that limit" points at another arrow's text), it states the conclusion (the favouring ends) and not what makes the change, it uses "base grammar", which a reader with no knowledge of the theory cannot place, and it omits the one premise this law adds to exit 1's: `start : favours g`, the rule favours the winners at the start. The fixed condition says the premises in the places' words. That this is the grammar's statement of exit 1's arrow, and should be drawn as one arrow carrying two laws, moves to the note.

condition_en: Where the rule as judged favours the winners whatever the judging and the lead, the hold is in place by the step after the second re-setting, whatever rule and judging it started with.
condition_zh: 只要不论怎么评、领先多少，评出来的规则都偏向赢家，那么不管起初的规则和评法是什么，到第二次重定规则之后的那一步，局面就已经锁住。
evidence: Lean, experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/ClosedCapture.lean line 468-476, docstring: "Where the rule read favours at every reading and share, every course is locked from the step after its second reading step, whatever rule and reading it starts with." Statement: `(formed : ReadsShare P MQ mind) (uniform : ∀ q x g, favours (read q x g)) {c : S × (G × Q)} {r r' : Nat} (first : reads r = true) (second : reads r' = true) (lt : r < r') : Locked (both MG MQ) (fun p : G × Q => favours p.1) (readers read mind) (paced (byRule f) (readers read mind) reads c (r' + 1))`. Record closed-capture.md law 6 adds: "within a loop whose every level reads only the share, what leaves is a change of the law". dynamics.json transition kind: "pace bound".
note: No arrow. The readers' FROM ends (several-ways; shaping-pays) are not in the law: its start `c` is arbitrary (any lead, any rule, any judging), and nothing about several ways being live or about bending the rule paying appears among its premises. The premises already put the loop in the setting where both the rule and its judging are formed from the lead (`formed`, `readMono`) and favour at every lead (`uniform`); the law is how fast the hold is in place there: within two re-settings. A sufficient statement, not an iff, so "sufficient". Caveat on the place: this law has no coordinate for a loss at all (the Readers section is over S × (G × Q)), so by the letter of the tests it also meets holds-itself ("says NOTHING about a loss"); I put it in judged-inside because the two-level formation (rule AND its judging both from the lead) is what the law is about and what distinguishes it from RuleCapture.uniform_locks, of which it is the two-level case. One reader voted holds-itself as destination, two judged-inside.

condition_en: Those not ahead register the loss; the rule still favours the winners, who are the fewer.
condition_zh: 落后的一方把损失算进去时，规则仍偏向赢家，而赢家人数比他们少。
evidence: experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/ClosedCapture.lean, Thinned.kept_iff (line 900), hypotheses `(at_r : reads r = true) (past : N ≤ (course fB u v w N reads c r).1.2) (fav : favours (course fB u v w N reads c r).2)`, statement `(∀ k, Locked order favours (poolRead u w) ((course ... (r + (1 + k))).1.1, (course ... (r + (1 + k))).2)) ↔ (course ... r).1.1.other ≤ (course ... r).1.1.carrier`; docstring: "where they are fewer, it is not locked at the next step." Same file, Thinned.rule_read (line 886): `(course fB u v w N reads c (r + 1)).2 = pool u w (course fB u v w N reads c r).1.1`; Drawn.mirror_favours_iff (line 674): `favours (pool u w x) ↔ x.other ≤ x.carrier`. dynamics.json exit: "the course is not locked for good under the late pool from the next step on".
note: What is exact: with the winners fewer at such a step, the rule in force at the NEXT step leans to those not ahead (kept_iff's docstring; the statement itself gives only 'not locked at every later step', the next-step fact is rule_read with mirror_favours_iff). The law does not say it stays there. Whether it then holds the other way for good is turned_iff's question at the next re-setting (those not ahead still at least as many), and it can fail: winners 4 to 5 under a 4:1 rule, each side backing its own 4:1, gives a rule 21:24 for the others for one step, then 69:36 for the winners with the winners 336 to 120, and kept_iff then locks it for the winners for good (my arithmetic from select, rule_read and kept_iff; no Lean declaration states this example; the related record the-lock-draws-its-readers-out has a proved course of the same shape, Drained.strong_undone). So the map should not read this arrow as arrival for good. The law holds at any step where the rule is re-set with the loss past its bound, not only the first; 'register' here means the step is one at which the rule is re-set. Premises not in the condition: once they register the loss, those not ahead back their own side exactly as strongly as the winners back theirs (mirror), the winners' own judgment favours them strictly, the loss grows at least one a step; the rule is the count-weighted sum of the two sides' judgments. No axiom. Not shown: that any actual rule is such a pool (record, 'Does not show'). The readers' three-way split: noticers-gone as the origin does not fit, since the law's premise is that the others are present and read the loss; past-turning-back is the kept side of the iff, which is transition 2.
fixed_why: The arrow felt -> cost-counts survives: the from-state (loss past its bound at a step where the rule is re-set, rule in force still favouring the winners) meets felt's test, and the destination meets cost-counts' test by its own words ("not locked there"): Thinned.rule_read gives the rule at the next step as the pool at the counts there, and Drawn.mirror_favours_iff says that pool favours the winners exactly where they are at least as many, so with the winners fewer the next rule in force leans strictly to the others, because the others now read the loss. Direction and strength (exact, an iff) are right. Two things are wrong and I fix them. (1) The condition says "first register the loss". The Lean has no "first": kept_iff holds at ANY reading step with the loss past its bound and the rule in force favouring the winners (`at_r : reads r = true`, `past : N ≤ ...`, `fav : favours ...`). "First" invites the inference that the first registration settles the outcome, and it does not: by my own arithmetic from the stated laws (not a Lean declaration), winners 4 to others 5 under a rule 4:1 for the winners, each side backing its own 4:1, read every step, gives rule 21:24 at the next step (leans to the others), but the winners have meanwhile grown to 16:5, the rule after that is 69:36 for the winners, and kept_iff applied at that step locks it for the winners for good. So the same course passes through this arrow and then through transition 2's arrow. (2) The condition omits the law's premise that the rule in force still favours the winners. The note must also say that this arrow is one step: staying needs turned_iff's condition at the next re-setting. I checked my step model against the Lean witness (inTime 1: counts 4:8, rule 12:33, as in Thinned.inTime_majority).

condition_en: Each side backing its own equally, the pooled rule leans to whichever side is at least as many among its makers.
condition_zh: 双方各自同样偏向自己时，合起来的规则偏向定规则的人里人数不少于对方的那一边。
evidence: ClosedCapture.lean line 674, mirror_favours_iff: "(hc : w.carrier = u.other) (ho : w.other = u.carrier) (strict : u.other < u.carrier) : favours (pool u w x) ↔ x.other ≤ x.carrier"; docstring: "Against a mirrored reading the majority decides ... the pool favours the carriers exactly where they are at least as many as the others." Line 694, mirror_disfavours_iff: "disfavours (pool u w x) ↔ x.carrier ≤ x.other". Record law 3 (readers-drawn-from-the-selected.md): "Against a mirrored reading the counts decide".
note: A tipping count (even numbers among the rule's makers) inside one place, with no loss in the statement: the place's test says a flip from one side to the other with no loss counted stays inside it. All three readers agree. The two lemmas are statements about which way the pooled rule leans at given counts; they contain no step in time and no hold by themselves (the hold comes from through_locks / agreeing_stays in the same record). At exactly even counts both hold: the rule gives each side alike.

condition_en: Those not ahead register the loss; the rule still favours the winners, who are no fewer.
condition_zh: 落后的一方把损失算进去时，规则仍偏向赢家，而赢家人数不比他们少。
evidence: experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/ClosedCapture.lean, Thinned.kept_iff (line 900): hypotheses `(at_r : reads r = true) (past : N ≤ (course fB u v w N reads c r).1.2) (fav : favours (course fB u v w N reads c r).2)`, statement `(∀ k, Locked order favours (poolRead u w) (...(r + (1 + k))...)) ↔ (course ... r).1.1.other ≤ (course ... r).1.1.carrier`. Thinned.read_late_kept (line 830) docstring: "the course is locked under the late pool at every step from `r + 1` ... while the loss, read by every other reader, grows by at least one a step." For the second law, Thinned.turned_iff (line 918): hypothesis `(dis : disfavours (course fB u v w N reads c r).2)`, statement `(∀ k, Locked (reverse order) disfavours (poolRead u w) (...(r + (1 + k))...)) ↔ (course ... r).1.1.carrier ≤ (course ... r).1.1.other`. theories/becoming/results/records/readers-drawn-from-the-selected.md law 6: "the rule in force favouring the carriers, the course is locked for good exactly where the carriers are at least as many as the others there; the rule in force favouring the others, it is locked the other way for good exactly where the others are at least as many."
note: This item carries two laws. The decision above is kept_iff's kept side: the objection comes too late. The law holds at any step where the rule is re-set with the loss past its bound, not only the first. The second law, turned_iff, is NOT a second arrow from felt: its premise is that the rule in force already leans to those not ahead (ties included). Record it as: stays, place cost-counts, strength exact, condition "The rule already leans to those not ahead, who register the loss and are at least as many." (zh: 规则已偏向落后的一方，他们把损失算进去时人数不比赢家少。), then it holds that way for good; where they are fewer it is not held that way for good. The premise does not say why the rule in force leans to them, so this is a law of cost-counts only where the lean came from the loss being registered (as one step after exit 1's arrow; the in-time witness runs exactly so: Thinned.inTime_majority at step 1, locked the other way from step 2). The entry's 'between' is two outcomes at such a step, not a change from one to the other, so both_ways is false. Record's caveat: "locked the other way says the carriers' share never rises again, not that it falls". Premises not in the condition: once they register the loss, those not ahead back their own side exactly as strongly as the winners back theirs (mirror); the winners' own judgment favours them strictly; the loss grows at least one a step; the rule is the count-weighted sum of the two sides' judgments, which stay fixed. No axiom. Not shown: that any actual rule is such a pool.
fixed_why: The main decision survives: felt -> past-turning-back, exact, one way. kept_iff's right-to-left half (through read_late_kept) says that at a step where the rule is re-set, the loss past its bound and read by every other reader, the rule in force favouring the winners, the hold is kept at every later step exactly where the winners are at least as many; that is past-turning-back's test ("kept for good although read"), and the from-state is felt's (loss reaches readers of the rule, rule not turned; felt's gloss: "it depends on how many they are and how early"). The entry's own 'between' (kept for good <-> held the other way for good) is rightly not drawn: no law takes a course from one to the other. Three fixes. (1) "first register" again adds what the Lean does not say (any reading step past the bound) and the condition omits the premise that the rule in force still favours the winners; see exit 1 for a course where the first registration finds the winners fewer and a later one keeps the hold for good. (2) The note proposes turned_iff as a second arrow felt -> cost-counts. Its premise is `dis : disfavours (course ... r).2`: the rule in force ALREADY leans to those not ahead (ties included) at the step. That is not felt's test ("the law does not yet say the rule has turned"), so felt is the wrong origin and no change between two places is stated: the law says when a rule already leaning the other way, the loss registered, holds that way for good. It should be recorded as 'stays' in cost-counts (whose test names "locked the other way under the reading of the loss"), exact, not as an arrow. Even that has a limit: the premise does not say WHY the rule in force leans to the others, so it sits in cost-counts only where that lean came from the loss being registered, as it does one step after exit 1's arrow. (3) The note should carry the record's caveat on ties and the premises; kept.

condition_en: Nothing comes back to the rule-benders alone, bending the rule costs them, and some of them are present.
condition_zh: 没有任何东西只回到改规则的人自己手里，改规则又要付出成本，而且一开始就有人在改。
evidence: experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/RuleShaping.lean lines 285-292: "With nothing coming back to the shapers and a cost, the shapers' share falls strictly at every step of the run, the shapers present at the start." theorem nothing_back_falls (cost : 0 < c) (some : 0 < x.carrier) (n : Nat) : orbit(n+1).carrier * orbit(n).other < orbit(n).carrier * orbit(n+1).other, the orbit under select y (shaped a 0 p c pos). RuleCapture.lean line 479: order.le x y := x.carrier * y.other ≤ y.carrier * x.other (a comparison with the others, not a head count). Record theories/becoming/results/records/shaping-the-rule-selected-by-what-comes-back.md law 3: "With nothing coming back and a positive cost, the shapers' share falls strictly at every step of the run, the shapers present at the start".
note: What stays: at every step of the run the rule-benders lose ground to the rest (they become a smaller part of the whole). Their head count need not fall: each still leaves a + p ≥ 1 successors, and present_along keeps them present, so nothing here leads to 'ended'. No arrow: the statement has no earlier state; it is the shaping-costs test holding at every step under one fixed rule. The exit's "drops: ruleshaping-covers" names the premise of covering_locks whose absence defines this case; the crossing between the two places is drawn once, at transition 1 (favours_iff, disfavours_iff). All three earlier readers drew shaping-pays -> shaping-costs; the law does not show that change.
fixed_why: The decision holds: stays in shaping-costs, sufficient. I could not find an arrow in the statement. nothing_back_falls is a run under one fixed rule (shaped a 0 p c, cost positive) from any start with rule-benders present; it names no earlier place, and the crossing between pays and costs is already carried exactly by transition 1. It does not reach 'ended': present_along (line 271) keeps them present along the run. The fix is to the Chinese condition only. It appends a consequence the English does not have, 他们的人数每一步都在减少, and that is false as a head count: each rule-bender leaves a + p ≥ 1 successors, so their count does not fall; what falls strictly is their standing against the rest (carrier(n+1)·other(n) < carrier(n)·other(n+1)). The condition should state the premise only, and the note should say what stays in relative terms.

condition_en: What comes back to the rule-benders alone no longer covers its cost, whatever everyone gets alike.
condition_zh: 只回到改规则的人自己手里的那部分不再抵得上成本，不管人人都得到的那部分有多少；反过来抵得上了，就回到划得来。
evidence: Lean, RuleShaping.lean lines 158-178: "The rule after shaping favours the shapers (weakly) exactly where the cost is at most what comes back to them alone." theorem favours_iff : CarrierCounts.favours (shaped a s p c pos) ↔ c ≤ s; theorem disfavours_iff : CarrierCounts.disfavours (shaped a s p c pos) ↔ s ≤ c; favours_alike: "What comes to every member alike does not decide the direction". Record page law 1: "at a step the rule favours the shapers (weakly) exactly where c ≤ s and disfavours them (weakly) exactly where s ≤ c, whatever p comes to every member alike."
note: Direction follows the entry's between (from c ≤ s to s ≤ c); both directions are iff statements. The statement is at one step and static: which place holds is decided exactly by cost against what returns alone, and the crossing is a change in those two quantities, which the law does not itself produce. Both sides are weak, so at cost = return both hold; the place list puts that tie in shaping-pays ("at least what it costs"). That numbers actually fall strictly on the costs side needs shapers present (lt_select_iff, falls_strictly).

condition_en: Over a stretch, rounds paid before anything returns outweigh the rounds with a return; what all get counts.

condition_en: Where bending the rule returns much while its doers are at least as many as the rest and little while they are fewer, with the cost in between, each side of that count feeds itself, however often the rule is re-set from the count: starting at least as many, they gain on the rest at every step; starting fewer, they lose ground to the rest at every step. No law here shows a crossing from one side to the other.

note: Both theorems are implications from a start on one side (sufficient, not exact); each says that side keeps going its own way, and the companion laws say the start is never recrossed and the rule in force stays the one set on that side. So the law gives no passage between the sides, and the holds-itself test places a tipping count inside that place. What rises or falls is the rule-benders' standing against the rest; below the line their head count does not fall, they are outgrown. Read with the other two places: above the line bending the rule pays, below it costs, and each side holds. Readers split two (inside holds-itself) to one (shaping-costs -> shaping-pays, exact); the statements support the two.
fixed_why: The decision holds: inside holds-itself, sufficient. threshold_rises (567-573) and threshold_falls (600-606) are one-way implications from a start on one side, so 'exact' (two readers) would be an upgrade. No crossing is shown: threshold_from_above (478-484) and threshold_from_below (497-503) say the start is never recrossed, and threshold_rule_above/below (519, 543) say the rule in force stays the one set on that side. The rule is rebuilt from the count of its own winners (byBack over thresholdBack, line 458) and no loss outside the count is mentioned: the holds-itself test, 'on either side of a tipping count'. The one reader's shaping-costs -> shaping-pays arrow is not in any statement. The fix is to the plain sentence. 'Starting as the minority they fall at every step' reads as a falling head count, and under threshold_falls the rule-benders' count does not fall (each leaves a + lo + p ≥ 1; threshold_present_below keeps them present); the law is that they lose ground to the rest. 'Majority' should be 'at least as many' (thresholdBack: `if x.other ≤ x.carrier then hi else lo`, the tie counts as above). The law's 'under every schedule of reading' is added in plain words.

note: The start is this dynamic's own hold (the run before step N is this dynamic's run, favoured at its start and so held by drawn_locks). That those not ahead come to count the loss at all is the model's premise, not something a law here decides: no law gives holds-itself -> felt. The felt -> cost-counts leg is the same test as loss-read-in-time-by-the-others' exit (turned_iff), so on the map this is that arrow's entry from holds-itself, not a second independent way out. 'Twice running' is the law's premise that the rule is judged again at the step they start counting and at the next; the test is taken at the second, on the numbers one step on. The failing branch (kept_early_iff, deadline) belongs to that other dynamic and leads to past-turning-back. The iff is on the condition, not a reverse change.
fixed_why: The arrow itself stands; only the condition's wording is corrected. I read the statement in /Users/ren/theories/experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/ReadInTime.lean (theorem turned_early_iff, line 319): hypotheses `fav : CarrierCounts.favours (DrawnShaping.drawn a p c hi lo pos x)`, `at_N : reads N = true`, `at_next : reads (N + 1) = true`; conclusion `(∀ k, Locked (reverse CarrierCounts.order) CarrierCounts.disfavours (DrawnShaping.drawnRead a p c hi lo' pos) ...) ↔ CarrierCounts.disfavours (DrawnShaping.drawn a p c hi lo' pos (DrawnShaping.drawnCourse a p c hi lo pos reads x (N + 1)).1)`. The start is this dynamic's hold (theorem `early`: up to step N the joined run IS this dynamic's run; `fav` with lo ≤ hi gives drawn_locks), and the end is 'locked the other way under the late reading', which is the cost-counts test word for word. Direction right; strength exact copied from the exit; not both ways (the iff is on the condition, no law returns from cost-counts). Two faults in the plain condition: (1) the law's premise that the rule is judged again at step N and at step N + 1 (at_N, at_next; the exit's own words 'steps N and N + 1 reading') was left out, and 'early' was put in, which is not a premise but a consequence (late_never_falls); (2) the Chinese carried 'ties included' and the English did not. The corrected condition carries the two rejudgings and the tie in both languages.

condition_en: members replaced one at a time by chance: every rule-bender can be lost, or everyone become one

The law is a lower bound on the weight of such histories from any mixed count (on either side of the tipping count): it shows the hold can be left by chance with positive weight and gives no rate. Nothing newly counted, no new person with a say (the exit's edge: "no new reader and no change in what is read"). The exit cites lost_ge; the fixing half is fixed_ge.

condition_en: Where the rule-benders with a say see more coming back than the cost and the others with a say see less, a tipping count divides two holds: the rule favours the benders exactly where their number stands to the others' at least as (cost minus what the others see) to (what the benders see minus cost). A run that starts under the rule as judged at its start stays on its side at every step: above the count the benders' numbers rise at each step, below it they fall.
condition_zh: 在有发言权的人里，改规则的人看到的回报高于代价、其余的人看到的低于代价时，有一个临界人数把两种“撑住”分开：改规则的人与其余人之比不低于（代价减其余人所见）比（改规则者所见减代价）时，规则偏向他们。从“按起点人数评出的规则”出发的进程，每一步都留在自己那一边：临界人数之上，改规则的人步步增多；之下，步步减少。

Record /Users/ren/theories/theories/becoming/results/records/shaping-read-by-readers-drawn-from-the-selected.md laws 2-4, and its 'Does not show': "starts not under the rule read there (a rule in force against the reading can carry the share across the mass, RuleCapture.Reversed.not_absorbed)".

A run that starts under a rule other than the one judged at its start, returns or cost that change with the numbers, and chance are outside these laws; chance is exit 2. One reader drew shaping-costs <-> shaping-pays: the two sides are where the benders' numbers fall and rise, but no law here moves a run from one to the other.
fixed_why: Decision (inside holds-itself, exact) stands: no arrow was wrongly withheld. critical_iff (DrawnShaping.lean line 227) and critical_mass_iff (line 310) are static iffs on where a count stands; both ends of the data's 'between' are holds ('the course is locked in their favour' / 'locked the other way'), no loss is counted, and the holds-itself test names this case ('on either side of a tipping count ... A flip from one side to the other with no loss counted stays inside this place'). An arrow shaping-costs <-> shaping-pays would read as runs crossing, and drawn_locked_either says the opposite for runs started under the rule judged at their start. The fix is one sentence of the plain text: 'No run crosses the count without chance or an outside push' says more than the law. drawn_locked_either is only for a run 'from the rule read at its start', with constant cost and returns; the record's own 'Does not show' lists 'starts not under the rule read there (a rule in force against the reading can carry the share across the mass, RuleCapture.Reversed.not_absorbed)', which is neither chance nor an outside push. Replaced by the law's premise.

condition_en: the cost moves between at most what each kind with a say sees returning and above both
condition_zh: 代价在“不高于两类有发言权的人各自所见的回报”与“高于两者”之间变动
evidence: /Users/ren/theories/experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/DrawnShaping.lean: favours_everywhere_iff, "(∀ x, CarrierCounts.favours (drawn a p c hi lo pos x)) ↔ c ≤ lo ∧ c ≤ hi", docstring "With no hypothesis on the readers, the rule read favours the shapers at every share exactly where the cost is at most what the others among the readers read as coming back and at most what the shapers among them read"; disfavours_strictly_everywhere_iff, "(∀ x, (drawn a p c hi lo pos x).carrier < (drawn a p c hi lo pos x).other) ↔ lo < c ∧ hi ≤ c", docstring "At `hi = c`, `lo < c`, the shapers are favoured at no share, however many." Record /Users/ren/theories/theories/becoming/results/records/shaping-read-by-readers-drawn-from-the-selected.md law 3.
note: A tipping in a parameter: it moves a run only if the cost or what is seen returning changes. Exact boundaries: pays at every count exactly where the cost is at most what the others see AND at most what the benders see; costs at every count exactly where the cost is above what the others see AND at least what the benders see ('above both' in the short condition leaves out the edge where the cost equals what the benders see). The two ends are not complements: where the others see less than the cost and the benders more, a tipping count decides (transition 1, inside holds-itself); where the benders see less than the cost and the others at least it, the entry lists the case as open. So the two-way arrow passes through a third regime unless both kinds see the same return. These two laws take no hypothesis on those with a say and assert no hold.
fixed_why: The arrow, its two ends, both_ways and strength stand; the condition is corrected. favours_everywhere_iff (DrawnShaping.lean line 257): "(∀ x, CarrierCounts.favours (drawn a p c hi lo pos x)) ↔ c ≤ lo ∧ c ≤ hi" is the shaping-pays test at every count (what each kind sees returning covers the cost, ties included, matching 'their numbers do not fall'); disfavours_strictly_everywhere_iff (line 284): "(∀ x, (drawn a p c hi lo pos x).carrier < (drawn a p c hi lo pos x).other) ↔ lo < c ∧ hi ≤ c" is the shaping-costs test at every count. Each end has its own iff and both are listed places, so both_ways true is within the rule, and it is the same shape as the neighbouring dynamic's arrow between the same two places (RuleShaping.favours_iff / disfavours_iff), to which this reduces when both kinds see the same return (alike_favours_iff). Fault: the condition named one direction only ('the cost rises from ... to ...') on an arrow marked both ways. Reworded direction-neutral. What a map reader must also be told, kept in the note: the two ends are not complements. Between them lie lo < c < hi, the tipping-count regime of transition 1 inside holds-itself, and hi < c ≤ lo, which the entry lists as open; so the arrow is a change in cost or in what is seen returning that passes through a third regime unless both kinds see the same return. It moves no run by itself.

condition_en: Members replaced one at a time by chance: the weight of runs that leave the hold against its side (every rule-bender lost from above the tipping count, or everyone a bender from below it) is capped, and the cap shrinks by a factor for every step of distance from the tipping count. It caps that one end only: under chance a mixed membership does not last, and the rest ends on the hold's own side.
condition_zh: 成员一次换一个、凭运气：逆着撑住的那一边离开的情形（临界人数之上却一个改规则的人都不剩，或之下却人人都成了改规则的人）所占分量有上限，离临界人数每远一步，上限就再缩小一截。它只限住这一头：凭运气，混合的局面不会长久，其余的都落到撑住的那一边。

(fixed M) k (j + 1) ≤ (j + 1) * ups (up M a p hi lo) j n * whole M a p c hi ^ k. Module docstring: "as a share, at most `t` times the product of `down / up` across the stretch, each count above the mass multiplying it by less than one where it favours strictly." Record /Users/ren/theories/theories/becoming/results/records/drawn-shaping-drawn-one-at-a-time.md law 2: "over rounds of M + 1 steps the histories still varied vanish geometrically", and law 4.
note: An upper bound on how much weight exit 2's change carries against the hold's side; the change itself is exit 2 (lost_ge, a lower bound). Best shown as a weight on exit 2's arrow, not as a second arrow. The cap is (distance to the top) times one factor per count of distance, each factor the others' weight over the benders' there, below one where the rule favours the benders strictly; near the tipping count, or where chance is strong against the pull, the cap can be loose or exceed the whole and then says nothing. It is an inequality, not an iff, and does not say the hold is never left: by the fixation law the mixed hold is left under chance, toward one end or the other.
fixed_why: No arrow was wrongly withheld and the place is right; one clause is added so 'stays' is not read as more than the law. lost_above (DrawnReplacement.lean): "ups (up M a p hi lo) s n * valueBy M (whole M a p c hi) (up M a p hi lo) (down M a p c) (stay M hi lo) lost k (s + n) ≤ t * ((M + 1) * (a + c + p)) ^ n * whole M a p c hi ^ k" under `mass : down M a p c s ≤ up M a p hi lo s`, and fixed_below its mirror, are upper bounds on the weight of exit 2's change in the direction against the hold's side. An upper bound cannot carry an arrow (two readers' holds-itself -> all-on-one with strength 'bound' is not among the strengths and would read as 'things go there' where the law says how seldom). Strength sufficient is right for an inequality. But the same record's law 2 (fixation) says "over rounds of M + 1 steps the histories still varied vanish geometrically": under chance replacement a mixed population does not last, so what the law keeps is the SIDE (which end is reached), not the place. The sentence now says so. The cap also carries the factor t (the distance to the top) and can exceed the whole when near the tipping count; kept in the note.

condition_en: The others count the loss while judgments taken together still go against the winners, this round and next.
condition_zh: 其他人把损失算进去时，大家的判断合起来在这一轮和下一轮仍不利于赢家。
evidence: experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/ReadInTime.lean, docstring of turned_iff: "at a reading step `r` at which the loss has reached its bound and the late reading favours the others at the share there (ties included), `lo' ≤ hi`, the step `r + 1` reading too: the course is locked the other way under the late reading at every step from `r + 2` exactly where the late reading favours the others at the share at `r + 1`". Statement: (∀ k, Locked (reverse CarrierCounts.order) CarrierCounts.disfavours (DrawnShaping.drawnRead a p c hi lo' pos) ...(r + 1 + (1 + k))...) ↔ CarrierCounts.disfavours (DrawnShaping.drawn a p c hi lo' pos (course ... s (r + 1)).1.1). Record theories/becoming/results/records/loss-read-in-time-by-the-others.md, law 3, same words.
note: From is 'felt': the premise `past : N ≤ loss` is that the others already read the loss, and nothing yet says the rule has turned.
